_description: Worked example of how exp_001 (completed) and exp_002 (in_progress) map onto actual Firestore collections, per the Module Contract's security boundary (§8): correct answers, clue text, and the full-resolution reveal image live ONLY in the *_private collection, which Firestore rules make unreadable by any client — it is read exclusively by Cloud Functions using the Admin SDK. Clients only ever read puzzle_experiences (public projection) and their own puzzle_progress document. Collection names are namespaced with a puzzle_ prefix per the Contract's future-extensibility convention (§9), so a future host platform can add quiz_*, timeline_*, etc. without collision.

puzzle_creators/cre_001._readWrite: creator can read/write only where creatorId == request.auth.uid

puzzle_experiences/exp_001._readWrite: publicly readable by anyone holding a valid resolved token for this experience; writable only by the owning creator
puzzle_experiences/exp_001.welcomeNote: Hey Annie, three years ago today I promised to make every day feel like this one. Before I say anything else, I need you to prove you remember us as well as I do. Nine pieces, nine memories. Ready?
questionPrompts: Where did we go on our very first date?
What did I spill on you the first time we met?
What's the name of the restaurant where I proposed?
What song played during our first dance at the wedding?
What nickname did I give you in our first month of dating?
Which city did we honeymoon in?
What's our favorite weekend breakfast spot?
What do we call each other on bad days?
What's the one thing I promised you on our wedding day?
puzzle_experiences/exp_001._note: Note what is NOT here: correctAnswer, acceptedVariants, clues, the real revealImage path, completionMessage, and partnerHelpChallenge all live in the private doc below. questionPrompts is safe to expose because a prompt alone reveals nothing.

puzzle_experiences_private/exp_001._readWrite: no client access whatsoever — Firestore rule is allow read, write: if false; only Cloud Functions (Admin SDK) touch this document
puzzle_experiences_private/exp_001.completionMessage: You remembered every single one — of course you did. Happy anniversary, my love. Here's to the fourth year, and every one after it.
puzzle_experiences_private/exp_001.partnerHelpChallenge: Stuck? Ask Vikram directly — but he's only answering if you bring him a cup of filter coffee first. ☕

clues: It's a big green space in the city we met in.
We shared street-side cotton candy there.
It has a famous bandstand where we sat and talked for two hours.
It was hot, and I apologized way too much.
It came in a paper cup from the campus canteen.
You still tease me about my clumsy hands.

puzzle_experiences_private/exp_001._note: Only q1-q2 shown here for brevity — the full document contains all 9, matching 03-puzzle-experiences.json.

puzzle_progress/exp_001._readWrite: created and updated only by the recipient session resolved from this experience's token; no read/write access for other tokens or unauthenticated requests without the matching token
puzzle_progress/exp_001._note: Full 9-piece map matches 04-progress-examples.json — truncated here for brevity.

puzzle_experiences/exp_002.welcomeNote: Happy birthday, Priya! Before your cake, you've got homework — nine questions about us. Let's see how much attention you've actually been paying. 😉

puzzle_events/evt_0009._readWrite: write-only from Cloud Functions; read access restricted to the owning creator (their own experiences) for the Insights screen

tokenResolution._description: How a share link resolves to an experience without exposing the Firestore document ID relationship directly (Contract §8: token must never be derivable from the document ID).
tokenResolution.resolutionFlow: Client calls the resolveShareToken Cloud Function with the token from the URL. The function looks up shareTokenHash in puzzle_experiences_private (server-side only), confirms a match, and returns the public puzzle_experiences/{experienceId} projection plus a short-lived session reference the client uses for subsequent calls. The raw Firestore document ID (exp_001) is never derivable from the token pzl_7f1c9ad2b6e34a08 by design — they are unrelated random values.
